messages.author: 011e5e2cc7d3b3de
messages.subject: set Context  to generic
parts:
Hi All,
     
Instead of context = "CpG". I want to use a file where I have all the three context CPG,CHH,CGH ? Is there anyway doing it in methylkit?  What is the option? I have created a file from bismark and using the generic read function with pipeline arguement.

e.g

methylObj = read(listOfFiles, sample.id = list("test","ctrl"), treatment = c(1,0),assembly = "hg19", header = FALSE, context = "CpG", resolution = "base", pipeline = list(fraction = TRUE, chr.col = 1, start.col = 2, end.col = 2,coverage.col = 5, strand.col =3, freqC.col = 4))


I want to set context, which should be able to handle all the contexts together.


many many thanks

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] set Context to generic
parts:
Dear Raza,

I am not sure if one can do this in methylKit yet. But before considering to do that, one may consider the fact that methylation atleast in human genomes is highly contextual. This means that methylation is mostly (~99%) is observed at CpG only and not in other contexts. Also  note that the functions that operate of CpGs can not be used in other contexts eg., merging strand coverage from + and - strand. 



Regards,
Kalyan

messages.author: 38c56d0e82a34280
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] set Context to generic
parts:
All the functionality will work fine- the context string is not used in any of the calculations. I've done a one or two analyses where I've brought in all contexts- I've labeled the context 'CNN" in methylKit.

One word of caution- eDMR was tested against the CpG context. Although mathematically the operation is the same (need to find a distance cutoff to define regions), use all contexts may significantly change the results.
